related_questions.snippet: Take Over-The-Counter Medications Antivirals are most effective if started within the first 48 hours of symptoms. If used accurately, they can shorten the duration of illness by about 24 hours and decrease the risk of complications, especially in high-risk populations.

related_questions.question: How to speed up COVID recovery?

text_blocks.snippet: To help speed up COVID-19 recovery, focus on getting adequate rest, managing symptoms with over-the-counter medications, and taking precautions to avoid spreading the virus. The average recovery time for mild cases is typically one to two weeks.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on getting adequate rest, managing symptoms with over-the-counter medications, and taking precautions to avoid spreading the virus

list.title: Rest and Sleep:
list.snippet: Prioritize getting more sleep than usual, exceeding the recommended 7-9 hours for adults.

list.title: Symptom Management:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help with fever and body aches.

list.title: Isolation and Hygiene:
list.snippet: Avoid strenuous exercise, wear a mask, and avoid sharing personal items like dishes and towels.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: Regularly check your symptoms and seek immediate medical attention for any emergency.

list.title: Caregiver Safety:
list.snippet: If you have a caregiver, they should also be healthy and mask up when in the same space as you.

related_questions.question: How long should you stay home once you test positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: You should isolate for at least 5 days counting from the day you began feeling sick (Day 0 is the day you began feeling sick; Day 1 is the next day). If you have no symptoms, then isolate for 5 full days after the day you tested positive (Day 0 is the day you took your positive test; Day 1 is the day after).
